At the outset, let me clarify that this extensive feedback below  is on the hospital (which I visited because of my appointment with Dr Ramakrishnan). It is NOT on Dr Ramakrishnan. All in all, a cold, indifferent vive.

Horrible moments of truth with Kokilaben.
Horrible memories seldom leave. An important lesson in customer experience which might be worth learning for your hospital.
6. Only one set of elevators take us down to the ground floor from the first floor OPD. But there's no communication to that effect.
6. Dr Aparna is a wonderful Doctor. The Doctor though is only one element in the hospital experience.

Don't know whether this feedback makes any difference to the hospital; nevertheless, I have shared.

If nighttime anxiety is keeping you awake, remember that you don't have to just "deal with it." It has a medical explanation, and more importantly, it can be treated.

Ever wonder why your mind waits until your head hits the pillow to remind you of everything you’ve ever worried about? 🧠💤
It’s not a personal weakness—it’s actually biology. During the day, the brain is flooded with external stimuli: work, conversations, scrolling, and daily noise. This constant "busyness" acts as a natural mute button for your brain's alarm system, the amygdala.
But when the lights go out and the room goes silent, the distractions disappear, and those suppressed fear signals get amplified.
If nighttime anxiety is keeping you awake, remember that you don't have to just "deal with it." It has a medical explanation, and more importantly, it can be treated.

Hair pulling is not simply a "bad habit." For many people, it is a treatable mental health condition called Trichotillomania (Hair Pulling Disorder).

People with trichotillomania often experience:
✔ Repeated pulling of scalp hair, eyebrows, eyelashes, or beard hair
✔ Difficulty controlling the urge despite wanting to stop
✔ Temporary relief after pulling
✔ Visible hair thinning or bald patches
✔ Feelings of embarrassment, guilt, or low confidence

This condition can affect children, teenagers, and adults. Stress, anxiety, boredom, perfectionism, or emotional distress may worsen symptoms.

The good news is that effective treatments are available. Evidence-based approaches such as Habit Reversal Training (HRT), Cognitive Behaviour Therapy (CBT), and appropriate medications when needed can significantly reduce hair-pulling urges and improve quality of life.

🧠 ADHD: Myths vs Facts

ADHD is one of the most misunderstood neurodevelopmental conditions. Unfortunately, myths and misconceptions can delay diagnosis, increase stigma, and prevent individuals from getting the support they need.

❌ Myth: ADHD is caused by poor parenting.
✅ Fact: ADHD is a neurodevelopmental condition with strong genetic and biological influences.

❌ Myth: Only hyperactive children have ADHD.
✅ Fact: Many individuals, especially girls, may primarily struggle with inattention and organization.

❌ Myth: Children outgrow ADHD.
✅ Fact: While symptoms may change over time, ADHD often continues into adolescence and adulthood.

❌ Myth: ADHD means low intelligence.
✅ Fact: People with ADHD can be highly intelligent, creative, innovative, and successful.

Understanding the facts helps us move away from judgment and toward support, early intervention, and effective treatment.

Have you heard any of these myths before? Let us know in the comments. 👇

🚨 Common Signs of ADHD in Children 🚨

ADHD is more than just being energetic or easily distracted. It is a neurodevelopmental condition that can affect attention, behavior, emotional regulation, and daily functioning.

Some common signs include:
✔️ Difficulty paying attention
✔️ Excessive fidgeting or restlessness
✔️ Acting without thinking
✔️ Trouble following instructions
✔️ Frequent forgetfulness
✔️ Disorganization
✔️ Easily distracted by surroundings
✔️ Emotional outbursts or frustration

Every child may show some of these behaviors occasionally. However, when these difficulties are persistent, occur across different settings (home and school), and interfere with daily life, a professional evaluation may be helpful.

Early identification and support can make a significant difference in a child’s academic, social, and emotional development.

What is ADHD?

It can impact academic performance, work, relationships, and daily functioning, but with proper understanding and support, individuals with ADHD can thrive.

🔹 Inattentive Type
Often appears as distractibility, forgetfulness, difficulty staying organized, and trouble sustaining attention. These individuals may seem quiet, daydreamy, or “lost in thought.”

🔹 Hyperactive-Impulsive Type
Characterized by excessive movement, restlessness, impulsive decisions, frequent interruptions, and difficulty waiting one’s turn.

🔹 Combined Type
The most common presentation, involving symptoms of both inattention and hyperactivity-impulsivity.

ADHD is not caused by poor parenting, laziness, or lack of discipline. Early identification and evidence-based treatment can make a significant difference in helping children and adults reach their full potential.

Square Breathing (Box Breathing): A Simple Technique for Panic Attacks

When anxiety or panic starts to rise, square breathing can help slow your breathing and calm your body’s stress response.

⬜ Step 1: Breathe in through your nose for 4 seconds
⬜ Step 2: Hold your breath for 4 seconds
⬜ Step 3: Breathe out slowly through your mouth for 4 seconds
⬜ Step 4: Hold your breath again for 4 seconds

Repeat this cycle for 1–3 minutes or until you feel calmer.

Why it helps:
During a panic attack, breathing often becomes rapid and shallow. Square breathing encourages slow, controlled breaths, which can reduce physical symptoms such as a racing heart, dizziness, and feelings of panic.

Remember: Panic attacks are uncomfortable but not dangerous. Controlled breathing can help your body regain a sense of balance and control.
